html:
Brazzaville, the capital of the Republic of the Congo, grew from a French post founded in 1880 on the north bank of Malebo Pool, facing Kinshasa across the Congo river.

It became the capital of French Congo and in 1910 of French Equatorial Africa. In 1940 the colony rallied to de Gaulle, and Brazzaville served as the capital of Free France until Algiers took over. The Brazzaville Conference of 1944 met there.

The town grew around African quarters such as Poto-Poto and Bacongo, known for music, painting and the dandies of La Sape. It was badly damaged in the civil war of 1997, and has since been rebuilt with oil money.
